timeline.text: Chest x-ray: right lower lobe opacity
Chest x-ray: pulmonary vascular congestion, small bilateral effusions

notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient seen and examined at bedside. 89-year-old female admitted for community-acquired pneumonia. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.49, bnp 1607, creatinine 1.03, hemoglobin 13.1, platelets 275, sodium 141, wbc 5.5; vitals dbp 67-70, heart_rate 83-88, map 90-92, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 15-16, sbp 130-137, spo2 96, temp 36.6-36.9
Day 0 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV; Chest x-ray: pulmonary vascular congestion, small bilateral effusions; Chest x-ray: right lower lobe opacity; Furosemide 40 mg IV; Transthoracic echo: LVEF 26%, global hypokinesis
Assessment and plan: Community-acquired pneumonia. Acute systolic heart failure.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 0.99, hemoglobin 13, platelets 280, sodium 141, wbc 5.9; vitals dbp 65-71, heart_rate 83-88, map 87-92, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 15-16, sbp 130-137, spo2 95-97, temp 36.6-36.8
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV; Furosemide 40 mg IV
Assessment and plan: Community-acquired pneumonia. Acute systolic heart failure. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 89-year-old female, length of stay 4 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Community-acquired pneumonia. Acute systolic heart failure. Follow up with primary care in one week. Patient seen and examined at bedside.
